conviction_note: Small net lean up. The run-rate (H1 +14%, Q2 +15%, Trauma & Deformity +26%, 3P Hip sets deploying from late June) points to Q3 revenue around $69.5-70.5m against an implied bar near $68.5m, and the last four prints were bought (+3.8 to +9.8%). Against that: the reiterated ~$25m adj EBITDA guide needs about $16m in H2 versus $9.0m in H1, the largest holder (Squadron, ~24%, with a director on the board) sold about 677k shares mid-quarter, and HCA's Q3 surgical volumes were down. abs_move 7.5 is the name's own median reaction (no usable option chain); p_up 55 because the lean rests on run-rate arithmetic, not a disclosed number. impact_sum (+0.2) and impact_scaled (+0.75) agree in sign and are both small.
bar: FY2026 revenue guide $265-269m (raised 2026-08-04, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001425450/000142545026000066/kidsq22026earningsrelease.htm); FY consensus $267.0m from 8 analysts, range $265.9-267.8m, i.e. the guide midpoint (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/kids/forecast/, targets updated 2026-09-15). No Q3 consensus could be sourced. The implied Q3 bar of about $68.5m is my inference: H2 implied by the guide is $135.1-139.1m after H1 of $129.9m, and Q3 2025 ($61.2m) roughly equalled Q4 2025 ($61.4m), so H2 splits about evenly. Q3 2025 comp: $61.2m ($60.7m ex-7D). Because the Q3 bar is single-sourced and inferred, the quarter-level findings are capped small.
positioning_check: No current short-interest print was reachable: the Nasdaq API returned 503. The latest found is 948,112 shares on 2026-03-13, days to cover 5.94 (https://equibles.com/stocks/kids/shortinterest). That is about 3.6% of 26.1m shares outstanding, or about 4.8% of the float after Squadron's ~6.2m shares, and about 4 days on the current 232k 20-day average volume. MarketBeat showed 6.7% of float and 7.3 days on 2025-09-15. Short interest is moderate, not crowded. The options chain is unusable (open interest 73, ATM spread 170% of mid), so there is no skew. Tape: +6.0% over 20 days, +2.7% over 5 days, 8.9% below the 52-week high and 64.8% above the low. Squadron Capital, the largest holder and controller of a board seat, sold about 677k shares at $21.01-25.75 between Aug 24 and Sep 10; the stock bottomed near $21 and has since recovered to $24.13.

findings.finding: The run-rate points to a Q3 beat and a third straight raise. Revenue grew 13% in Q1 ($59.4m), 15% in Q2 ($70.5m) and 14% in H1 ($129.9m). Trauma & Deformity grew 26% in Q2, 3P Hip sets only began deploying in late June, and most of the ~$10m set deployment falls in Q3. Holding H1's 14-15% on the $61.2m Q3 2025 comp gives $69.8-70.4m, against an implied Q3 bar of about $68.5m that the guide midpoint and the $267.0m FY consensus imply. The company raised the FY guide by $2m in each of Q1 and Q2 on beats of about $2m. International is the easy comp: +6% in Q3 2025 against +22% in each of Q1 and Q2 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat-and-raise prints were bought: Q2 2026 beat (70.5 vs 68.2 per MarketBeat) with a $2m raise, +6.85%; Q1 2026 beat with a $2m raise, +3.78%; FY25 prelim/guide (Jan 2026), +9.83%; Q4 2025, +7.76%. When the line missed, the stock fell: Q3 2025 prelim miss with a guide cut, -9.19% (2025-10-09); Q2 2025, -11.34%.
findings.why_not_priced: FY consensus sits exactly at the guide midpoint ($267.0m, range $265.9-267.8m, none above the $269m top), so the street has not modelled continuation of the H1 run-rate, which would put FY at about $270m+. If the street had priced it, consensus would sit at or above the guide top, as it did before Q3 2025. The stock is still 9% below its 52-week high after the Squadron selling.
findings.independence: The FY consensus is a separate source: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/kids/forecast/. The Q3-heavy set deployment and the H2 positive FCF commentary come from https://quartr.com/events/orthopediatrics-corp-kids-q2-2026_onZfKuTJ. Both rest on the same company disclosures.

findings.finding: No Q3 pre-announcement was issued before the Oct 27 print. In 2025 the company pre-announced a Q3 revenue miss and cut guidance on Oct 9 (-9.19%). It also pre-announced FY revenue in January 2026. Its EDGAR filings since Aug 5 2026 are only Form 4s, a Form 144 and Squadron 13D/As, with no 8-K, and the only October release is the Oct 13 date announcement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-10-09 pre-announced miss moved -9.19%; the next day the full print moved -2.66% (2025-10-28).
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference from absence and is sized small for that reason. A company that pre-announced its last large miss three weeks before the print has not done so this year. Had the market feared a repeat, the stock would not have risen 6% over 20 days into the print.
findings.independence: The Oct 13 date announcement with no preliminary numbers: https://www.biopharmawatch.com/news/KIDS/orthopediatrics-q3-2026-financial-results. The 2025 pre-announcement precedent: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1425450/000142545025000108/kidsprelim3q25v4-finalsa.htm

findings.finding: Squadron Capital is the largest holder (25.0% before the sales, 23.8% now), and its president David Pelizzon sits on the board. Squadron sold about 677k shares between Aug 24 and Sep 10 2026, about 2.6% of shares outstanding and about $15m, at weighted averages from $25.75 down to $21.01. That was mid-Q3, and the Form 4 shows no 10b5-1 box marked. The stated reason is 'to provide additional capital for its other portfolio businesses.' The 13D/A states no Item 4 change, so further sales after the print remain possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print with a comparable Squadron sale was found. The stock fell from about $25.75 to about $21 over the selling window and has since recovered to $24.13.
findings.why_not_priced: The sales are public and the price absorbed them: a fall to $21 and then a full recovery. What is not priced is the overhang. A holder that sells post-print in the open window could resume after this release, which would cap any post-beat follow-through. The 'other portfolio businesses' reason argues it is liquidity-driven rather than informed, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: The earlier tranche (Aug 24-Sep 1, 375,131 shares): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1425450/000119312526378878/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml (same filer, same series).

findings.finding: The adj EBITDA guide of ~$25m was reiterated, not raised, when revenue was raised. H1 adj EBITDA was $9.0m (Q1 $2.2m, Q2 a record $6.8m), so H2 needs about $16m, roughly $8m a quarter against a record quarter of $6.8m. Most of the ~$10m set deployment lands in Q3, and the FCF-breakeven promise needs positive FCF in H2 after $3.1m used in Q2 and cash fell to $47.9m from $62.9m. A Q3 EBITDA shortfall, or wording that softens EBITDA or FCF, is the downside path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2025 print moved -11.34% and Q3 2025 -9.19%/-2.66%. Those reactions were on revenue and guidance cuts; no separate EBITDA-only miss is identifiable in the history.
findings.why_not_priced: Coverage frames the story on revenue raises. The H2 EBITDA step-up implied by an unchanged ~$25m is arithmetic no one quotes. Revenue running above guide at about 74% gross margin should fund it, so this is a risk inside a guide the company stands behind, not a forecast miss. It is sized small.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001425450/000142545026000066/kidsq22026earningsrelease.htm) with finding 1. Those are the same documents read on a different line, revenue there and EBITDA here, so they are not double-counted.

findings.finding: HCA's Q3 2026 release, out on the print day, shows same-facility inpatient surgeries -1.4% and outpatient surgeries -3.7% while admissions rose 2.7%. That continues Q2's surgical declines (-2.3% inpatient, -3.4% outpatient), which were tied to a payer-mix shift toward uninsured patients. It is a read on the US procedure and payer environment in the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific; KIDS has never cited adult hospital-system volume as a driver.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out the same day and is a weak proxy. Pediatric orthopedics runs mostly through children's hospitals, a heavily Medicaid mix, and KIDS's own US growth was +14% in Q2 while HCA's surgeries were already falling. Hence the small size.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, not company-confirmed. It is partly contradicted by J&J MedTech's Q3, where orthopaedics trauma was a growth driver: https://capital.com/en-gb/news/johnson-johnson-q3-sales-rise-on-medtech-growth-lifts

findings.finding: J&J reported Q3 2026 in mid-October, after KIDS last spoke on Aug 4. Its MedTech growth was led partly by orthopaedics trauma, a read on trauma procedure demand, KIDS's largest segment at 75% of Q2 revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: This is adult trauma at a mega-cap, the transmission to pediatric share gains is weak, and it is snippet-only (the exact orthopaedics number was not retrieved from the 10-Q). So it is tiny.
findings.independence: Cuts against the HCA proxy above. J&J 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000197/jnj-20260927.htm

outside_window.finding: Squadron Capital may resume open-market sales of its remaining 6.2m shares (23.8%) after the print opens the trading window. That would be an overhang after the first session.

baseline_tension: There is no skew. The modest +6% 20-day run-up and the positive reaction history to beat-and-raise prints agree with the small up lean, so this does not cut against the tape. The baseline's own warning that the history may be mis-built is answered: these are confirmed releases and pre-announcements, and the sweep marked the history trustworthy.
lessons_applied: Rule 6: the Q3 bar is inferred and single-sourced (only the FY consensus sits at the guide midpoint), so the run-rate finding is capped at +1.2, down from +1.5.
Rule 5: the no-pre-announcement finding is an inference from absence, so it moves from +0.7 to +0.4.
Rule 7: short interest was checked before the negatives (moderate, about 4-6 days to cover, March 2026 data), so the Squadron finding moves only slightly, -0.8 to -0.7.
Rule 1: the reaction history pays beat-and-raise prints on this name, so the reaction is not vetoed; p_up moves from 56 to 55 for the inferred bar.
